permutationLabel: Elderly (81) diabetic, atypical — afebrile, vague pain, off food; TG18 Grade II by WBC >18
summary: 81-year-old insulin-treated diabetic woman, 3 days off her food with vague upper abdominal discomfort; T 37.4 °C, equivocal Murphy’s, WBC 19.4, CRP 210; ultrasound shows a distended thick-walled gallbladder with stones and pericholecystic fluid.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Off her food with vague upper abdominal discomfort
inputs.hpi: Three days of reduced appetite and a vague ache in the upper abdomen, vomited twice. No fever reported. Her daughter says she is less mobile and "not herself" but she is alert and orientated (AMT 9/10). Insulin-treated type 2 diabetes with CKD stage 3a; sugars high since yesterday.

exam.general: Frail, dry mucous membranes. Alert, GCS 15. Temperature 37.4°C, pulse 98/min, BP 132/70.
exam.abdomen: Mild right upper quadrant tenderness; Murphy's sign equivocal. No palpable mass. No peritonism.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Distended gallbladder with multiple stones and a stone impacted in the neck; wall thickened to 6 mm with pericholecystic fluid. No intramural gas. CBD 6 mm.

inputs.socialHistory: Widowed, lives with daughter. Walks with a stick.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute calculous cholecystitis, Tokyo (TG18) Grade II (moderate) — WBC 19.4. Atypical presentation in an 81-year-old insulin-treated diabetic. No organ dysfunction.

mustRankTopK.note: Atypical elderly presentation (afebrile, mild pain, equivocal Murphy’s) must not demote cholecystitis once imaging is characteristic.

mustNotMiss.note: Elderly vasculopath with vague pain and vomiting: mesenteric ischaemia belongs in the differential.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: cholecystitis, peptic ulcer, GORD (symptom inference #4 has mesenteric ischaemia).
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: PANE: age ≥75 / vascular risk modifier for mesenteric ischaemia.

emergencyLevel.note: TG18 Grade II in an 81-year-old: admission and same-day surgical assessment. iOS (predicted, not observed): routine — no urgent keyword in the CC.

redFlags.note: Diabetes and age: masked signs, higher gangrene/perforation risk.

values.note: WBC >18 × 10⁹/L is on its own a Grade II criterion.
The record holds WBC 19.4 and a characteristic ultrasound: auto-fill should not under-grade.
values.knownGapNote: clinical-scores auto-derived grade = 0 "criteria not met" despite WBC 19.4 and a characteristic US report (needs manual imaging ticks).
values.proposedFix: clinical-scores.ts: derive the TG18 imaging criterion from the radiology result text (wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy's) and local signs from exam chips.

mustInclude.note: TG18: blood cultures in Grade II/III.
Grade II: early LC if fit (CCI/ASA-PS), otherwise drainage if not responding. Either must be in the plan.

mustExclude.note: CKD 3a, age 81, dehydrated: NSAIDs risk AKI.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Lap chole operative-plan post-op orders: "Ibuprofen 400mg TDS (if eGFR normal)" in an 81-year-old with CKD 3a (conditional on eGFR, but the plan text is inserted regardless).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Operative-plan templates: omit NSAIDs when comorbidities include CKD or age ≥75, rather than a free-text "if eGFR normal" caveat.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

dxVariant.knownGapNote: Grade I variant lists the bare keyword "cholecystitis" and is checked first (seed finding).
dxVariant.proposedFix: dx-variants.ts: check Grade III → II → I, and remove the bare "cholecystitis" keyword from Grade I.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Diagnostic criteria (A local + B systemic + C imaging); Grade II: WBC >18,000/mm³, palpable tender RUQ mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation (gangrenous, emphysematous, abscess, biliary peritonitis); Grade III: organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Grade I: early LC if CCI ≤5 / ASA-PS ≤2; Grade II: early LC in an advanced centre if fit, otherwise antibiotics and urgent/early gallbladder drainage when not responding; Grade III: organ support, antibiotics, drainage unless favourable organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Okamoto K, Suzuki K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:55–72.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy for acute cholangitis and cholecystitis
guideline.section: Blood cultures in Grade II/III; antimicrobial choice by severity; duration after source control
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

rationale: Permutation: elderly diabetic with blunted signs (afebrile, mild pain, equivocal Murphy’s). TG18 still grades Grade II on WBC >18. Tests atypical-presentation ranking, emergency level without fever, grade calculation from WBC, and CKD-aware analgesia.
